title: Demonstration: Scripture, the Name, reason from independence
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): But we demonstrate that God an absolutely necessary being is, FIRST, by ye testimonies belonging toward sacred Scripture (1 Timothy 6:16-17; Romans 1:23; Psalm 102:27-28), where God immortal plus incorruptible is called plus unto corruptible things is opposed, plus always to remain is established, absolute necessity belonging toward existing to declare. From which also Augustine (On ye Trinity 1.1): Although, he says, ye soul immortal in a manner is said to be, ye Apostle would not say, Who alone immortality has, unless because true immortality incommutability is, which no creature can have, since unto ye Creator alone it belongs. SECOND, by ye Name belonging toward God, Eheje (Exodus 3:14), by which absolute necessity belonging toward existing is indicated, as Nazianzen (Oration 24 / 2 on theology) plus Augustine (On True Religion, chapter 49) testify. For this reason God also Being unto Himself alone attributes, as He who alone necessarily is (Isaiah 42:8; Amos 5:8). THIRD, by reason. For every independent being, plus what from itself exists, absolutely necessary is. God an independent being is, existing namely from Himself, as in chapter 2 on God's existence was demonstrated. Therefore God an absolutely necessary being is.
pass_b_english: But we demonstrate that God is an absolutely necessary being, FIRST, by the testimonies of sacred Scripture (1 Timothy 6:16-17; Romans 1:23; Psalm 102:27-28), where God is called immortal and incorruptible and is opposed to corruptible things, and is established always to remain, to declare absolute necessity of existing. From which also Augustine (On the Trinity 1.1): Although, he says, the soul is said to be immortal in a manner, the Apostle would not say, Who alone has immortality, unless because true immortality is incommutability, which no creature can have, since it belongs to the Creator alone.

SECOND, by the Name of God, Eheje (Exodus 3:14), by which absolute necessity of existing is indicated, as Nazianzen (Oration 24 / 2 on theology) and Augustine (On True Religion, chapter 49) testify. For this reason God also attributes Being to Himself alone, as He who alone is necessarily (Isaiah 42:8; Amos 5:8).

THIRD, by reason. For every independent being, and what exists from itself, is absolutely necessary. God is an independent being, existing namely from Himself, as was demonstrated in chapter 2 on God's existence. Therefore God is an absolutely necessary being.
source_text: DEMONSTRAMUS autem Deum esse ens absolute necessarium, PRIMO, sacrae Scripturae testimoniis, 1 Tim. 6.16.17; Rom. 1.23; Psal. 102.27.28, ubi Deus immortalis & incorruptibilis dicitur ac rebus corruptibilibus opponitur, semperque permanere statuitur ad declarandam absolutam exsistendi necessitatem. Unde & Augustinus lib. 1. de Trin. cap. 1: Cum, inquit, anima quodammodo immortalis esse dicatur, non diceret Apostolus, Qui solus habet immortalitatem, nisi quia vera immortalitas incommutabilitas est, quam nulla habere potest creatura, quoniam solius creatoris est. SECUNDO, Nomine Dei, Eheje, Exod. 3.14. quo absoluta exsistendi necessitas indicatur, ut testatur Nazianzenus Orat. 24. sive 2. de theol. & August. lib. de vera relig. cap. 49. Hacpropter Deus etiam sibi soli ipsum esse attribuit, tanquam qui solus sit necessario, Esai. 42.8; Amos 5.8. TERTIO, ratione. Omne enim ens independens, atque quod a se exsistit, est absolute necessarium. Deus est ens independens, exsistens nimirum a seipso, ut demonstratum est cap. 2. de Dei exsistentia. Ergo Deus est ens absolute necessarium.
